bib.title: Understanding the LLM Twin Concept and Architecture (LLM Engineer's Handbook, ch. 1)

question: How should an end-to-end LLM product (the LLM Twin) be scoped as an MVP and architected so that data, training and inference stay modular?
contributions: Defines the LLM Twin product and its MVP features
Applies FTI plus a data collection pipeline to a four-component LLM Twin architecture with a logical feature store

limits: No experiments, data or numbers: the chapter is product planning and architecture, so nothing in it measures pretraining data or objectives.
Pretraining is not discussed; the model is fine-tuned from an open-source LLM chosen later in the book.
The LLM Twin is framed as a thought experiment for a three-person team; tooling is left to later chapters.
Web print of the chapter (O'Reilly, dated 12/20/25); figures are not in the text.
practices: Design ML systems as feature, training and inference pipelines joined only through a feature store and a model registry (The solution).
Keep the architecture model-agnostic and data-centric so models can be swapped (Why not use ChatGPT).
Group collected data by category (articles, posts, code), not by source platform, so a new ETL can be plugged in (Data collection pipeline).
Use a logical feature store (vector DB plus versioned artifacts) when a specialised store is not worth the cost (Feature pipeline; Final thoughts).
Store best hyperparameters after experimentation to enable continuous training (Training pipeline).
Keep a manual approval step before promoting a model to production (Training pipeline).
Send queries, RAG-enriched prompts and answers to a prompt monitoring system (Inference pipeline).
Scope the MVP to a complete end-to-end user journey with no half-built features (What is an MVP?).
